A todo list that lets you rank objectives and provides suggestions of what to work on next based on that ranking. Good if you have litterally 100 tasks and sub tasks, or 20.

This one might be harder for people to figure out how to use without a few hints.

So the most obvious part is that if you want to add a new task to your list you would add it to the part that says 'add', and hit submit.

What you do next is (and really this list if for people who have at least 6 things to work on), is you drag the suggestions it gives you by how soon you want to be reminded about that task. If you drag it below the line it signifies that you want to remove it. The top task is then added to your notebook, to the right, as the thing you are working on.

That notebook is also a persistent scratch pad. If you write in it and go to another machine it will be there so it's a handy way to send notes from one machine to the next, and to take notes on the things you work on.

I personally just write DONE next to something I finish so it also acts as a journal of everything I've worked on.

It helps me keep busy and busy doing things in roughly the right order.

If you have a task that isn't very important and you shouldn't do right away but you still want it on your bucket list it's easy to just rank it lower relative to other tasks and you will be reminded about it eventually. That's better than putting it on a physical todo list that will eventually get thrown away.
